title: Learning How to Learn
summary: A short, practical course on how memory works and the study techniques that cognitive science actually backs — spacing, retrieval practice, interleaving, and elaboration. Ships as the Learning Hub's bundled example course (generated by the course-builder pipeline).
prerequisites: None — just bring something you're currently trying to learn so you can apply each technique.

modules.title: How Memory Works
modules.summary: Before techniques, the model: why you forget, and the difference between getting information in and getting it back out.

lessons.title: The Forgetting Curve
objectives: Describe Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve in plain language
Explain why review timing matters more than review volume
Predict what happens to recall without reinforcement

materials.title: The forgetting curve, flattened by review

lessons.title: Encoding vs. Retrieval
objectives: Explain why re-reading feels effective but isn't
Define 'desirable difficulty' and why it helps

modules.title: Evidence-Based Techniques
modules.summary: The four techniques with the strongest research support, and how to actually run them.

lessons.title: Spacing & Interleaving
objectives: Identify when interleaving helps and when it hurts

materials.title: Spread it out, mix it up
Dunlosky et al. (2013) — techniques review
materials.note: The landmark review that rates each technique's evidence.

lessons.title: Retrieval Practice & Elaboration
objectives: Run a retrieval-practice session from memory
Combine techniques into a weekly study loop

materials.title: Optional: deep-dive audio overview
